system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “[STANDARD]”, “FINAL” and “agreed” labels have no effect unless reflected in an actual agreement or authority from Wattlebridge. The disclosure package must also be refreshed from **22 September 2026** through signing and Completion.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | Meaningful recourse—target **50% of price / AUD 12m**, or equivalent W&I/escrow protection, with separate higher caps for protected categories. | **Reject 20% as the default without alternative protection; propose 50%.** A AUD 4.8m ceiling may leave Buyer bearing most loss from material warranty failures. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, with only excess recoverable. | Lower de minimis (e.g. **AUD 10,000**), related claims aggregated, and a **tipping basket** of no more than AUD 120,000–150,000. | **Counter with AUD 10k / AUD 120k tipping thresholds and aggregation.** The Seller’s structure suppresses smaller recurring SaaS liabilities and permanently transfers the first AUD 250k to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims expire **18 months after Completion**; Seller seeks the limitation for all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with longer bespoke periods for tax, title, IP, indemnities and covenants. | **Seek 24 months and reject extension of that limit to all Claims.** Eighteen months may expire before two full post-Completion reporting/audit cycles reveal problems. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same **20% cap and 18-month period** as general warranties. | Liability up to **100% of price**, no thresholds, and at least **six years** (or no contractual limit) for authority, ownership, title and encumbrances. | **Require a separate fundamental warranty regime.** Buyer must have full recourse if Seller lacked capacity or did not convey the shares it was paid for. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions purport to apply to **all Claims**; no express fraud carve-out is offered. | Express carve-out for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, dishonesty, wilful misconduct and deliberate concealment, unaffected by caps, thresholds, time bars or exclusive remedy. | **Insert an overriding fraud/deliberate-concealment carve-out.** Seller must not obtain contractual protection for intentionally false or concealed information. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, registers and public records, without admission of materiality or liability. | Only matters **fairly and specifically disclosed** against identified warranties, in sufficient detail to understand their nature, scope and likely financial effect; frozen indexed data-room copy and update through Completion. | **Delete general data-room/public-record disclosure and require specific fair disclosure.** Dumping documents on Buyer should not qualify warranties where the relevant risk was not clearly identified. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No Claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. | Preferably no knowledge qualification; failing that, only actual knowledge of named senior Buyer personnel, without enquiry, constructive knowledge or adviser imputation, and not applying to indemnities, title or fraud. | **Reject constructive and adviser-imputed knowledge.** Due diligence should inform the acquisition, not silently waive negotiated contractual protection. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Seller gives reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent despite unverified conditions in clause 11.3. | Final unconditional consent, with all related conditions satisfied, as a true **Condition Precedent** in form satisfactory to Buyer; no deemed satisfaction or waiver without Buyer consent. | **Do not Complete without effective Bluefen consent or an expressly agreed price/holdback solution.** Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and loss or impairment would be material. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding; release/discharge may be delivered **after Completion**. | Facility repaid and all guarantees and security released **at or before Completion**, using an agreed payout letter and funds-flow direction; releases as Completion deliverables. | **Make simultaneous repayment and discharge mandatory.** A post-Completion promise is inconsistent with a debt-free acquisition and exposes the Company to continuing lender security. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | AUD 420k of Completion bonuses are “a matter for Seller” but omitted from funds flow; payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unaddressed. | Seller bears the bonuses and every associated tax/on-cost; amounts paid or fully funded at Completion and treated as leakage/debt-like if retained by the Company. | **Add the grossed-up liability to funds flow and deduct/fund it dollar-for-dollar.** Completion-triggered Seller transaction costs must not reduce the value of a debt-free/cash-free business. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific unpaid **AUD 180k SOW3 fee**. No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is provided. | Payment and written confirmation of transfer before Completion, plus a specific indemnity covering ownership defects, infringement, remediation, replacement and third-party claims—not merely the fee. | **Require cure as a Completion deliverable and broaden the indemnity.** Paying AUD 180k alone does not ensure that essential Project Materials validly vest in the Company. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary incident, possibly involving 1,240 records; no admission of breach, access, notification duty or loss, and apparently left under the general regime. | Completed forensic/legal assessment, preservation and remediation, required notifications, continuing cooperation, and a specific indemnity for all pre-Completion incident costs and liabilities with enhanced cap/survival and escrow if unresolved. | **Do not accept disclosure alone; require investigation, remediation and specific protection.** The uncertainty concerns regulatory, customer, security and reputational exposure that arose before Buyer ownership. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110k renewals (AUD 330k total) characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Confirm necessity, termination rights, service periods, accrual and timing; no entry/renewal outside ordinary course without consent; proper treatment in working capital, leakage or price adjustment so Buyer does not pay twice. | **Reserve the issue pending contract and accounting diligence and hardwire the price treatment.** “Ordinary course” does not establish whether the costs are accrued, avoidable or already reflected in the price mechanics. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | Caps, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to Claims of every nature unless expressly excluded. | Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, IP, specific indemnities, debt/leakage, completion obligations, covenants, equitable relief and fraud. | **Reject a single omnibus limitation regime and draft an express claims hierarchy.** Different risks require different caps, survival periods and remedies, and broad language could neutralise negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Reliance on DD-012 share register showing Seller as holder of 100% of issued shares. | Independent verification through constitution, ASIC records, share certificates, allotment/transfer records, cap table, option/convertible checks, PPSR/security searches, beneficial ownership confirmation and releases. | **Make clean legal and beneficial title, free of encumbrances and third-party rights, a Completion condition and fundamental warranty.** A company-maintained register alone does not rule out security interests, competing rights or undisclosed dilution. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Seller treats tax and IP as settled under the 20%, 18-month general regime. | A standalone tax deed/indemnity with no basket and survival through applicable assessment periods; robust IP ownership/non-infringement warranties, higher caps and longer survival for core IP, plus specific protection for identified defects. | **Keep tax and IP expressly open and negotiate bespoke regimes.** Historic tax exposure and defective ownership of a SaaS company’s core IP can each exceed the proposed general cap and emerge well after 18 months. |

**Immediate Buyer priorities:** Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay title cure, bonuses/funds flow, and the unresolved privacy incident should be treated as Completion or price-protection matters—not merely warranty disclosures.
=== END ADVICE ===
